summary: Klamath NF lookout on a ridge above Seiad Valley, completed 1934 by a CCC crew; cab later moved to Ukonom Mountain; site today undocumented.

facts.design: Lookout cab reused from an older short tower, with some modification
facts.status_note: The cab was moved to Ukonom Mountain; no source describes the summit site now

access.note: Trip report describes a steep route up from Seiad Valley as one option; the writer came in along the PCT from the north

visit.trail_note: Writer came in along the PCT from the north, took a trail fork to the end of the ridge, and found an empty cinder block structure; the report also describes a steep initial ascent from Seiad Valley as one option

events.note: Construction completed by a CCC crew; materials packed in by mule from Seiad Valley
Lloyd Schmidt, a Klamath National Forest lookout, spotted a mountain lion about 100 feet from the station and shot it
Devils Fire burned to within 100 feet of the lookout building; lookout Louis Meiss refused to return

evidence.supports: Lookout built in 1934; CCC crew completed construction
evidence.quote: The Lookout construction was completed by CCC crew.

evidence.supports: January 1934 visit to look over the trail route for packing lookout material
evidence.quote: the trail route for packing Lookout material

evidence.supports: Packers carried 20-foot floor joists; trail had many switchbacks
evidence.quote: But the reason John and I were there was to help with those 20 foot long floor joists.

evidence.supports: Trail had as many as 25 switchbacks over about 3 miles
evidence.quote: There could have been as many as 25 switchbacks on that trail of some 3 miles in total distance.

evidence.supports: Lookout house taken off a short tower to be reused with modification
evidence.quote: The carpenters had previously removed the old lookout house from the short tower, which would be used again with some modification.

evidence.supports: July 1947 lookout Lloyd Schmidt spotted a mountain lion about 100 feet from the station and shot it
evidence.quote: Schmidt, a lookout for the Klamath National Forest, saw the animal about 100 feet from the station

evidence.supports: 1951 Devils Fire burned within 100 feet of the lookout building; Louis Meiss would not return
evidence.quote: Louis Meiss was run off Lower Devils Lookout by the Devils Fire, which burned within 100 feet of the Lookout building.

evidence.supports: Cab moved to Ukonom Mountain and set on a new base; no date given
evidence.quote: The cab from the Lower Devils lookout was transported to Ukonom Mountain and installed on a new base.

evidence.supports: Site is in the Klamath National Forest near Seiad Valley
evidence.quote: I was in the Klamath National Forest north of SR96 to climb a few CC-listed summits above the small community

evidence.supports: Lower Devils Peak is the end of a short ridge
evidence.quote: the end of a short ridgeline

evidence.supports: Trip report describes a steep initial climb from Seiad Valley as one route option
evidence.quote: with a steep, initial ascent to reach the ridgeline at Lower

evidence.supports: Trail fork ends at an empty cinder block structure
evidence.quote: empty cinder block structure is found.

evidence.supports: Writer asked whether the structure was an old lookout, unconfirmed

notes_for_editor: Two sources only: Kemnow's page (quoting the Klamath NF chronology and a 1934 John Buck account, plus a 1947 newspaper and 1951 chronology line) and one undated trip report. The cab move to Ukonom Mountain has no date and I found no source saying whether that cab still stands. A search snippet mentioned a 'Ukonom Lookout Tower' on 2017 fire maps; I did not open those PDFs, so it is not cited. The trip report's 'empty cinder block structure' may or may not be the lookout site; the story says so. The Ukonom Ranger District is administered by Six Rivers NF per a search snippet, unverified; a district office contact in Orleans could confirm the move date and the cinder-block structure. Record kind two_story is consistent with the FFLA index listing.
